# Dense

> A browser physics toy about density. Tungsten heavy-alloy cubes (90–97% W) against
> gold, copper, iron, titanium and aluminium — weighed on real instruments, dropped from
> a six-floor tower, crushed into things, and sunk in water, honey and mercury.

Everything in it is simulated rather than animated: a cube's mass comes from its alloy
density and its side length, and what happens next is a rigid-body solver's answer.

## What you can do

- **Sandbox** (`/`) — five material mats, and two line-ups: same size (wildly different
  mass) and same mass (wildly different size).
- **Weigh** (`/weigh`) — a digital scale and a balance. A gold cube and a tungsten cube
  of the same size read the same number, which is why gold-plated tungsten is the classic
  bullion fraud.
- **Drop** (`/drop`) — a winch, six floor materials, and crush targets from an egg to a
  cinder block. Verdicts are measured, not scripted.
- **Tank** (`/tank`) — buoyancy in water, honey and mercury. Four of the six metals float
  on mercury at exactly `ρ_cube / ρ_fluid` submerged; gold and tungsten sink, and come
  apart on the way down.

## Notes for machines

- Static site. No accounts, no tracking, no server-side state.
- Physics: three.js for rendering, Rapier for rigid bodies, a fixed 60 Hz step.
- Densities and material figures come from published sources and are documented in the
  repository, not tuned to feel good.
- Source: https://github.com/donth77/tungsten-cube-sim (MIT)
